crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Thematic Coding
children.blurb: Thematic coding is a qualitative analysis technique for identifying, organizing, and interpreting recurring patterns of meaning across text, interview transcripts, field notes, or other unstructured material.

children.name: Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation
children.blurb: Interview transcription and speaker separation covers the conversion of recorded qualitative interviews into text with reliable labels for each speaker.

children.name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
children.blurb: Finding patterns in lived experience refers to systematic analysis of qualitative data such as interviews, diaries, open-ended survey responses, and field notes to identify recurring themes, narratives, and meanings.

children.name: Ethnographic Synthesis
children.blurb: Ethnographic synthesis brings together findings from multiple ethnographic studies to build higher-order interpretations of cultural and social phenomena.

children.name: Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data
children.blurb: Combining qualitative and quantitative data means bringing together non-numeric evidence such as interviews, field notes, documents, or open-ended survey responses with numeric measures, counts, or model outputs.

sections.body: Qualitative analysis and mixed methods in AI research covers turning unstructured text, audio, and field notes into codes, themes, and comparisons. AI is actually doing this now through transformer models that transcribe interviews, cluster similar statements, and suggest labels for passages. Tools separate speakers in multi-person recordings and flag recurring phrases across dozens of transcripts. Some systems link coded segments to survey responses or demographic data for mixed methods work. This is not a future promise, it is routine in many research workflows.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Transcription and speaker separation are fairly reliable for clean audio in major languages, but they still stumble on overlapping speech, heavy accents, and domain jargon. Thematic coding assistance can speed up initial passes, yet the codes it proposes are often generic and need a human to check them against the research question. Pattern finding across lived experience works best when the corpus is large and the questions are narrow, and it fails quietly when meaning depends on context. Ethnographic synthesis remains the least automated part, because it requires judgment about culture, power, and silence that models do not have. Honest limits include hallucinated quotes, shallow interpretations, and a tendency to flatten minority viewpoints.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader starting with raw recordings would go to Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation to see what current tools can and cannot turn into text. From there, Thematic Coding explains how those transcripts become labeled categories, and Finding Patterns in Lived Experience shows what happens when many coded passages are compared. Ethnographic Synthesis moves from pattern lists to a coherent account of a group or setting, which is a different skill than clustering. Finally, Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data addresses the mixed methods promise, showing where numbers and narratives can be joined without losing either.
